caption: Figure 1: ( Overview .) Structured SSMs independently map each channel (e.g. 𝐷 = 5) of an input 𝑥 to output 𝑦 through a higher dimensional latent state ℎ (e.g. 𝑁 = 4). Prior SSMs avoid materializing this large effective state ( 𝐷𝑁 , times batch size 𝐵 and sequence length 𝐿 ) through clever alternate computation paths requiring time-invariance: the ( Δ , 𝑨 , 𝑩 , 𝑪 ) parameters are constant across time. Our selection mechanism adds back input-dependent dynamics, which also requires a careful hardware-aware algorithm to only materialize the expanded states in more efficient levels of the GPU memory hierarchy.

## Document Section 1
This figure is an overview diagram from the paper "Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces". It shows how the model maps input channels to output channels through a higher dimensional latent state. The diagram illustrates the mapping of input x to output y via the latent state h. It highlights the use of a selection mechanism to add input-dependent dynamics, which requires efficient memory usage on the GPU.

## Document Section 2
Text in figure: Overview, Structured SSMs, input x, output y, latent state h, D, N, Δ, A, B, C, Project, Selection Mechanism, GPU SRAM, GPU HBM.

## Figure Description
This figure illustrates different sequence modeling techniques. It shows three methods: Copying, Selective Copying, and Induction Heads. The Copying method demonstrates a straightforward copying of input to output. The Selective Copying method shows selective copying of specific input elements to the output. The Induction Heads method uses attention mechanisms to selectively copy input elements to the output.

## Figure Details
- Copying: Input: [blue, orange, red, green], Output: [blue, orange, red, green]
- Selective Copying: Input: [white, blue, white, orange, red, white, green, white, black, black, black, black], Output: [white, blue, white, orange, red, white, green, white, black, blue, orange, red, green]
- Induction Heads: Input: [blue, orange, red, green, white, white, black, black, black, black], Output: [blue]

caption: Figure 3: ( Architecture .) Our simplified block design combines the H3 block, which is the basis of most SSM architectures, with the ubiquitous MLP block of modern neural networks. Instead of interleaving these two blocks, we simply repeat the Mamba block homogenously. Compared to the H3 block, Mamba replaces the first multiplicative gate with an activation function. Compared to the MLP block, Mamba adds an SSM to the main branch. For 𝜎 we use the SiLU / Swish activation (Hendrycks and Gimpel 2016; Ramachandran, Zoph, and Quoc V Le 2017).
description:

It shows how these architectures are structured and how they differ from each other. The H3 block is the basis of most SSM architectures, while the MLP block is common in modern neural networks. Mamba combines these two by repeating a homogeneous block that includes an SSM and an activation function.
